name: British top-boost style (EL84 pair, no feedback)
notes: 60s British 'chime' style: bright, jangly, breaks up early and sweetly, very touch-sensitive. Its key features: EL84 power tubes, a tube rectifier (lots of sag), and NO global feedback loop (so there is no feedback block). Path: V1 -> volume -> top boost stage -> treble/bass circuit -> phase inverter with a 'cut' control -> 2x EL84. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): EL84 pair, no global negative feedback, tube rectifier, a cut control after the phase inverter, 12AX7 preamp stages. The treble/bass circuit is the tone stack block's top_boost style: 50 pF, 22 nF, 22 nF, 100k, 1M log treble and bass (from published summaries). UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: the fixed 10k where the mid pot would be; all bias values; the cut control as a 6 kHz low-pass; phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage); EL84 pair at 320 V into 8k with -13 V bias (a real one is cathode biased). POWER SUPPLY: GZ34 tube rectifier plus the winding, small filter capacitor, as 170 ohm into 32 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.)
